compiled_state.description:
## Context / Problem

Every other story in this epic is validated against fixtures and a stateful fake transport. That is
the right tier for each of them, but it cannot exercise the failure modes that only appear against a
real tracker: actual JQL evaluation over two projects, real per-project permissions and key
allocation, real issue creation, and — the one that matters most — whether a pass scoped to one
project can contaminate another. A multi-project bridge that is wrong in that direction writes real
issues into the wrong project, which is expensive to detect and worse to undo. This story is the
justified live canary the shared test-design standard allows for external-service mapping, run once
the functionality is otherwise complete.

## Approach

Rehearse the whole feature live, against an **isolated store copy**, with dry-run gating at every
step.

**Isolation comes first.** The rehearsal never runs against the production tickets branch. A copy of
the tickets branch is published to an encrypted S3 remote — the capability delivered by epic
`cf3c-1444-863e-49d7`, which is why this epic depends on it — and the rehearsal store points its
`sync.remote` at that copy. Before any mutating command, the harness asserts the configured remote is
the S3 copy and not the production remote, and aborts otherwise. This is a precondition assertion,
not a comment: it runs first and fails the test if the store is misconfigured.

**Dry-run gating is the contamination control.** Each scenario runs `bridge preview` first and
asserts the previewed mutation set contains **only** targets in the intended project, with an empty
intersection against every other configured project. Only then does `bridge sync` run. A preview that
names a target outside the intended project fails the scenario before anything is written — which is
the same fail-closed posture as the cross-project guard, applied at the harness level.

**Project configuration.** The mapping is loaded with the two live Jira Cloud projects, `REB` and
`DIG`, plus dummy projects that exist only in the mapping and never in Jira — these exercise the
"configured but empty" and "unknown to the tracker" paths without consuming real projects. Repo
configurations deliberately vary: one project mapped to a single repo, one mapped to two repos, and
one mapped to none, so the defaulting behaviour is observed across all three shapes rather than only
the common one.

**Cleanup is designed in, not bolted on.** Every issue the rehearsal creates carries a run-scoped
label. Cleanup is a single JQL sweep over that label across both live projects, and the run is not
considered finished until a follow-up query for the label returns zero issues in each project. The
label is generated per run so a failed earlier run cannot cause a later one to delete issues it did
not create.

## Scope

- `tests/external/live_multi_project/` (new) — the rehearsal harness and its scenarios
- `docs/jira-sync-setup.md` — the operator runbook for performing and cleaning up the rehearsal

## Testing

Tier: a live end-to-end rehearsal against real Jira Cloud, which the shared standard permits for
external-service mapping when a fake cannot reach the mechanism — here, genuine cross-project
isolation. It is gated to an opt-in external suite so ordinary CI never touches live Jira.

Scenarios, each preview-gated then applied:

- **Inbound from both projects.** An issue created in `REB` and one in `DIG` are both ingested in a
  single pass; each resulting ticket records the project it came from and the repos mapped to that
  project.
- **Outbound to both projects.** Two rebar tickets, one per project, each land as an issue in their
  own project and nowhere else.
- **Not-synced.** A ticket with an explicit empty project produces no issue in either project, and no
  outbound mutation naming it appears in the preview.
- **Legacy resolution.** A ticket with the project field absent syncs to the recorded legacy default
  and to no other project.
- **Repo-config variety, both directions.** Inbound tickets from the single-repo, two-repo and
  zero-repo projects receive exactly those repo lists; outbound tickets created under each config
  reach the correct project regardless of their repos value, confirming repos never influences
  routing.
- **Contamination guard, the negative control.** An update aimed at a project absent from the mapping
  raises `CrossProjectTargetError` in preview and writes nothing — verified by querying both live
  projects afterwards and confirming no issue changed.
- **Promote-only.** Setting a project on an unbound ticket then syncing creates the issue; attempting
  to change a bound ticket's project is refused and the existing binding is unchanged.
- **Capability stamp.** With two projects in the mapping, `.store-compat.json` carries
  `multi-project-bridge`, and a binary lacking that capability refuses to write to the rehearsal
  store.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The rehearsal aborts before any mutation if the configured remote is not the S3 store copy;
      checked by pointing it at a non-S3 remote and asserting it exits non-zero having written
      nothing.
- [ ] Issues created in `REB` and `DIG` are both ingested in one pass with the correct source project
      and repos recorded; checked by querying both live projects and asserting both tickets' fields.
- [ ] Rebar-created tickets targeting each project land in that project only; checked by querying
      both projects and asserting each issue exists in exactly one.
- [ ] A ticket with an explicit empty project creates no issue in either project; checked by a
      post-run query of both projects for the run label finding no issue for it.
- [ ] All three repo configurations produce the expected repos on inbound tickets and correct routing
      on outbound ones; checked per configuration.
- [ ] An update targeting an unmapped project is refused in preview and changes nothing live; checked
      by comparing both projects' issue state before and after.
- [ ] Every scenario's preview contained only targets in its intended project; checked by asserting
      an empty intersection against every other configured project for each preview.
- [ ] All issues created by the run are removed and a JQL query for the run label returns zero
      results in both `REB` and `DIG`; checked as the final step of the run.
